history.detail: Two release paths can strand notes (both reproduced by a probe; suites otherwise pass). (1) core/session.c:200-202: a sustain-up (MD_CMD_SUSTAIN value 0) refused at a completely full ring returns MD_ERR_CAPACITY but requests no emergency flush, although is_release() classes it as a release. Scenario: panel sustain down, note-on, note-off (note kept as released), ring saturated, sustain-up refused: after 10 blocks the voice still sounds and router.sustain[0][4] stays 1. Fix: also call request_flush(s, c->event.source) for a refused sustain-up (router release_source clears sustain), and add a test. (2) core/session.h:185 / session.c:189: flush_request is a uint8_t counter, so 256 refused offs for one source between two renders bring it back to flush_seen and the flush disappears (probe: 256 refused, request 0 == seen 0, voice stranded). Decision 002 asks for a coalesced flag. Fix: in request_flush, increment only when flush_request[source] == flush_seen[source] (one pending request per source), or use a sticky set-by-main/clear-by-ack pair; add a test that refuses more than 256 offs. Recommended, not blocking: a refused STOP or global PANIC at a full ring just returns an error and the sequencer keeps going; think about a coalesced stop/panic flag too, or say in the header that callers must retry. Checked and fine: ring fences, head/tail ownership, the bounded drain, flush taken before the drain and applied after it, the bank double buffer and main_live flip with ack, the sound slot, decode/base-vs-lock, tempo ranges, panic resetting effects. Ran: run_native.py session --sanitize on (PASS) and the full suite --sanitize on (12 suites PASS).

Read core/mixer.h/.c and tests/native/mixer_test.c against PLAN.md Mixer and effects and decision 002. Verified routing (insert1->insert2->level/pan/mute->dry; sends post-fader from panned l/r; wet-only returns to dry only, no return->send path; master over dry+returns), headroom by hand (inputs/insert/bus outputs clamped to 2^24, gain_apply x<=2^25 * 2^23 in int64, 4 tracks+2 returns <2^27, no division), partition independence (per-sample smoothers; mid-span settle exact since gain_apply(d,2^23)==d; post-zero processor calls in a fading-out span are inaudible and reset on re-enable), refusals check before mutation. Ran: tests/run_native.py mixer --sanitize on (8/8 PASS) and full suite --sanitize on (11 suites PASS). Non-blocking: (1) effect_in_use (mixer.c:149) compares state pointers only; a scratchpad probe showed two effects with partially overlapping state blocks both accepted into slots 0/1; use md_internal_overlap with state_bytes. (2) Processors can receive up to +48 dB (2^24); M3-03 effects must tolerate that or the mixer should narrow the range fed to them. (3) md_mixer_insert_idle returns 1 for a newly assigned unbypassed slot before its first span (harmless, wet is 0).

Blocking: the supported set says 'one rhythm key' and the evidence says 'the shipped module stays in the supported set', but module/seventies.c:486-489 lets the DRUMS page toggle any of ten rhythm keys plus all three extras while the band runs. Fix: add a variant (6 with the reachable maximum of rhythm keys and extras, i.e. what the DRUMS page allows) and report it. Probe: input 2^25 at level 16 gives 16384 out and clamped=0, where clamping first gave 8192 and clamped=512. The evidence's 'within the limit' wording covers this, and it is safe (no overflow, l still clamped), but the code comment should say the over-limit behaviour changed.
